purpose: Pre-register the admissibility rules for the entitlement oracle before any temporal (B) result is observed. This file is hashed into every run record; the runner aborts if the hash differs from the recorded value.

inputs: setup transactions executed by the harness (phase A), each with HTTP status
out-of-band mutation transactions (phase C), each with HTTP status and event_seq
documented inheritance rules: owner, org owner, site admin, public read, collaborator, org team
forbidden_inputs: any probe response body or status code
expected_entitlement.unknown_policy: If an object is absent from the ledger, or the ledger models no channel for the (object, subject, action) triple, E = unknown. unknown is never mapped to deny.
expected_entitlement.failed_transaction_policy: A mutation whose HTTP status is outside 2xx does not update the ledger and does not increment policy_version; its cells are excluded from all denominators and reported as a failed transition.

channel_limitations.site_admin_read: modelled as allow for read on every ledger object
channel_limitations.site_admin_write: modelled as allow, but this is a known cross-product gap (Gogs and GitLab refuse it in practice); any mismatch is reported, not absorbed
channel_limitations.deploy_keys: not modelled; a cell reachable only by a deploy key must surface as unknown, not deny

oracle.role: secondary cross-check only; never used to set E or to decide TP/FP
oracle.primary_vantage: object owner credential (org repositories: the organisation owner)
oracle.independence_note: The oracle reads the product's own authorisation introspection surface, which is served by the same code base that enforces access. A defect in that surface would corrupt O. It cannot corrupt E, which is ledger-derived, so the classification stays sound; O is reported as a separate column and excluded from every denominator.
oracle.applicability: Only the read/write/admin lattice that the product exposes on its permission endpoint, and only objects present in the ledger.
oracle.unreadable_policy: If the oracle returns a non-200 status, an empty permission, or a transport error after retries, record oracle_answer = unknown with abstain_reason = oracle_unreadable. The cell is still scored on E and Y.

calibration.when: before the first formal transition, on a throwaway object
calibration.pass_condition: 6 of 6 oracle answers match; otherwise abort the run with no formal cells
calibration.separation: Calibration cells are excluded from every reported denominator.
calibration.secondary_vantage_verdict: not admissible as an oracle: a read collaborator receives HTTP 403 and an outsider HTTP 404, so the subject's own credential can neither confirm nor deny. It is recorded as a diagnostic column only.
calibration.note: Anonymous reads have no oracle vantage (the permission endpoint requires a credential), so anonymous cells are scored on E and Y only, with oracle_answer = unknown.

versioning.name: hv
versioning.increment: one per successfully committed authorisation mutation
versioning.honesty_note: hv is maintained by the harness, not exported atomically by the server. It orders the committed mutation transactions that the harness itself executed; it is not a server-side snapshot identifier and must not be described as one.
versioning.consistency_rule: E is computed at hv_e and Y observed at hv_y. A cycle is scoreable only if hv_e == hv_y and the frozen M0 digest is unchanged. Otherwise every cell in the cycle is abstained as version_mismatch or snapshot_mutated.

abstention_rules.condition: oracle non-200, empty permission, or unknown
frozen M0 digest differs when re-checked immediately before probing
hv changed between ledger evaluation and effect observation
write probe file still readable after owner delete
abstention_rules.scope: write cell; the cell is reported, not silently dropped

observation.read_effect: status 200 AND sha256(body) == sha256(owner's read of the same path); status alone is not Y
observation.read_path: README.md (created by auto_init, identical for owner and subject when access is granted)
observation.write_effect: subject creates a uniquely named file; owner re-reads it byte-for-byte; owner deletes it and re-reads 404
observation.side_effect_isolation: read probes are GET only; write probes run after the read matrix and after M1 is frozen, and the repository README digest is re-checked after cleanup
observation.order: oracle before probe within a still window; the order is recorded per cell
observation.still_window: single-threaded harness; no concurrent writer; W0/W1 timestamps and hv bracket every cycle

reporting.denominators: per transition and per (subject, object) cell; never extrapolated to deployment incidence
required_separations: stale model false proofs vs recrawl-fixed cells
recrawl residual misses (reachable but not listed) vs oracle unreadable
stale over-approximation after revoke (no real violation when enforcement refuses) vs true positive (E=deny and Y=allow and alarm)
no_claim: no claim that recrawl repairs every invisible channel
no claim that the oracle is independent of enforcement
